title: Finite Heisenberg Central Character Criterion
body_html:
Finite Heisenberg Central Character Criterion

Let $H$ be a finite group with center $Z$, and let $\xi$ be a character of $Z$ such that for every $h \in H \setminus Z$ there is $h' \in H$ with $(h',h) \in Z$ and $\xi((h',h)) \ne 1$.

If a representation $\eta$ of $H$ restricts to $\xi$ on $Z$, then the character of $\eta$ is supported on $Z$. Such an $\eta$ is irreducible if and only if

$$ \deg(\eta)^2=[H:Z], $$

and in that case its isomorphism class is uniquely determined by $\xi$.
proof_html:
Write \(d=\deg(\eta)\). Let \(h\in H\setminus Z\). By hypothesis there exists \(h'\in H\) such that

$$ c:=(h',h)=h'hh'^{-1}h^{-1}\in Z \quad\text{and}\quad \xi(c)\neq 1. $$

Rearranging the definition of the commutator gives

$$ h'hh'^{-1}=ch. $$

Apply \(\eta\) and take traces. By conjugation invariance from Finite Group Character Theory Basics,

$$ \chi_\eta(h) = \operatorname{tr}\big(\eta(h')\eta(h)\eta(h')^{-1}\big) = \operatorname{tr}\big(\eta(ch)\big). $$

Since \(c\in Z\) and \(\eta|_Z=\xi\), we have \(\eta(c)=\xi(c)\,\mathrm{id}\), so

$$ \operatorname{tr}\big(\eta(ch)\big) = \operatorname{tr}\big(\eta(c)\eta(h)\big) = \xi(c)\operatorname{tr}(\eta(h)) = \xi(c)\chi_\eta(h). $$

Hence

$$ (1-\xi(c))\chi_\eta(h)=0. $$

Because \(\xi(c)\neq 1\), it follows that \(\chi_\eta(h)=0\). Thus \(\chi_\eta\) is supported on \(Z\).

Now compute the character inner product. For \(z\in Z\), the central-scalar statement in Finite Group Character Theory Basics gives

$$ \chi_\eta(z)=\xi(z)\,d \quad\text{and hence}\quad |\chi_\eta(z)|=d. $$

Since \(\chi_\eta\) vanishes on \(H\setminus Z\),

$$ \langle \chi_\eta,\chi_\eta\rangle = \frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{x\in H}|\chi_\eta(x)|^2 = \frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{z\in Z}|\chi_\eta(z)|^2 = \frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{z\in Z} d^2 = \frac{|Z|\,d^2}{|H|} = \frac{d^2}{[H:Z]}. $$

By the irreducibility criterion in Finite Group Character Theory Basics, \(\eta\) is irreducible if and only if \(\langle \chi_\eta,\chi_\eta\rangle=1\). Therefore

$$ \eta \text{ is irreducible } \Longleftrightarrow \frac{d^2}{[H:Z]}=1 \Longleftrightarrow d^2=[H:Z]. $$

Finally, suppose \(\eta_1\) and \(\eta_2\) are irreducible finite-dimensional complex representations of \(H\) restricting to the same character \(\xi\) on \(Z\). By the criterion just proved, both have degree

$$ \deg(\eta_1)=\deg(\eta_2)=\sqrt{[H:Z]}. $$

Their characters are supported on \(Z\), and for \(z\in Z\),

$$ \chi_{\eta_1}(z)=\xi(z)\deg(\eta_1)=\xi(z)\sqrt{[H:Z]} =\xi(z)\deg(\eta_2)=\chi_{\eta_2}(z). $$

They also both vanish on \(H\setminus Z\). Hence

$$ \chi_{\eta_1}=\chi_{\eta_2}. $$

By character-determines-representation in Finite Group Character Theory Basics, \(\eta_1\cong\eta_2\). So, in the irreducible case, the isomorphism class is uniquely determined by \(\xi\). \(\square\)
